newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman trying to repair EEP funding cuts.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman trying to repair EEP funding cuts.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday he was working with lawmakers in hopes of gaining larger funding for the Export Enhancement Program, the major U.S. export subsidy program.
"We are confident we can work through this problem," Glickman told reporters, adding that he wanted to push up the funding level for fiscal 1998.
A Senate subcommittee has set EEP at $150 million. The House Appropriations Committee has voted to allow $205 million for EEP. The administration requested $500 million.
"I'm worried about it," Glickman said, referring to the cuts. "EEP has become kind of a repository for every alternative program we can't find funds for somewhere else. That's disturbing to me."
The cuts are the result of budget pressures, he said.
"I think it's not good for us that it's falling that fast,"? Glickman added.
Glickman has said adequate EEP funding is needed in case the United States feels obligated to resume export subsidies as a countermeasure to practices by competitor nations.
